scenes.title: Facebook forms without GoHighLevel
scenes.narration: Let's connect your Facebook or Instagram form to Patient Pipeline without using Go High Level. We'll do it through Zapier, which passes the form response into the right campaign for us. You don't need to sign up for Go High Level for this route. You will need paid Zapier access for Facebook Lead Ads, so check that before we start. I'll take you through the setup and then show you how to follow your own test submission. The outside screens are labeled recreations; your account may look a little different, but we'll explain what you're looking for.

fields.label: Required
fields.value: Paid Zapier access for Facebook Lead Ads

scenes.checkpoint: No current price is promised. Check the plan available in your account.

scenes.title: Before we begin
scenes.narration: Before we get into the setup, have your actual offer handy. We'll use an example, but the information you enter should match what your own ad promises. You'll also need to be signed in, with permission to edit the connection. If you're wondering how to keep both accounts open, that little plus beside your browser tab opens another tab without closing this one. When we get to testing, use your own name and a phone you control, rather than patient information. Let your office know, too, because existing follow-up messages could run when you submit.

fields.label: Account access
fields.value: Patient Pipeline Lead Follow-Up and the source service

fields.label: Test information
fields.value: Your own name and phone; no patient information

scenes.checkpoint: Sign in before continuing. Never show passwords or private links.

scenes.title: Check Page and leads access
scenes.narration: Let's make sure we've got the right Facebook details before we open Zapier. Find the Page for this offer and the published Instant Form the ad uses, and keep both names handy. If you're advertising on Instagram, use its linked Facebook Page. The Facebook account we connect needs permission for that Page, the ad account, and leads access. If your business has customized leads access, the owner may also need to allow Zapier as a CRM. It's worth sorting that out now, because a missing permission won't be fixed by choosing a different form later.

fields.label: Access
fields.value: Manage Pages • Manage Ad Account • Leads Access

fields.label: Customized leads access
fields.value: Allow Zapier CRM access when required

scenes.checkpoint: Missing permissions cannot be fixed by choosing a different form.

scenes.title: Open a new campaign
scenes.narration: Let's start in Patient Pipeline. We're going to use Lead Follow-Up, rather than Reactivation, because we're setting up an offer that brings in new inquiries. Once you're in there, open Campaigns. This is how Patient Pipeline keeps each offer and its leads together, so your caller knows which conversation to have. Go ahead and click New Campaign. That brings us to the offer details. We'll keep using this same campaign for the connection and the test, so we don't end up looking for our test person in the wrong place.
scenes.checkpoint: You should be in Lead Follow-Up, with New Campaign open.

scenes.title: Choose the service
scenes.narration: Now that the offer form is open, the first thing I want you to look at is Service type. Click there to open the choices. I'm choosing Chiropractic because that matches the back pain offer we're using. Yours might be different, and that's completely fine. Just choose the service your ad is actually promoting, because that's what helps Patient Pipeline choose the right call script. Have a quick look at what's selected before we start typing the rest of the offer. We want the script to match the service, not just the name we're about to give it.
scenes.checkpoint: The selected service must match your ad.

scenes.title: Type a recognizable name
scenes.narration: Now that we've got the service selected, let's give the campaign a name your team will recognize. I'll click Campaign name and type Back Pain Relief, forty-nine-dollar New Patient Special. You don't have to use that wording. The important thing is that when someone on your team sees this name later, they'll know exactly which offer the person asked about. Keeping it specific also makes it easier for us to find the right campaign when we check the connection. Take a moment to enter yours, and then we'll add what the offer includes.

fields.label: Campaign name
fields.value: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special

actions.result: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special

scenes.checkpoint: Use the same campaign for setup, connection, and testing.

scenes.title: Enter what the offer includes
scenes.narration: Let's tell your caller what the person actually gets with this offer. I'm putting Consultation in the first row. We'll give each included item its own line, rather than squeezing everything into one sentence. To make room for another item, click Add a line. I'll put Examination in that next row, and then add Review of findings underneath it. Those are just our example's inclusions. Before you move on, compare your entries with the ad itself, because these details become part of what your caller says. We don't want to promise something your practice hasn't actually offered.
scenes.checkpoint: One real included item per row.

scenes.title: Choose Just Y, then type 49
scenes.narration: Now let's set the price wording your caller will use. Our example only needs to say what the offer costs, so I'm choosing the middle option, Just Y. Once that's selected, I'll click Offer price and type forty-nine. Have a look at the On the call preview underneath. That's where you can check the wording before anyone uses it. This doesn't change your software bill. If your ad really compares two prices, you'd use Normally X, now Y instead and enter both amounts. For our example, we'll leave this at Just forty-nine dollars.
scenes.checkpoint: Just Y selected • Offer price 49 • Preview Just $49

scenes.title: Save and connect leads
scenes.page: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special
scenes.narration: We've got the offer details in place now. You'll also see a place for an expiration or limited spots. It's fine to leave that blank if your ad doesn't have that restriction; we don't want to invent urgency. Take a moment to look back over what you've entered. When it matches your offer, click Save and Connect Leads. That saves the campaign and takes us to its connection setup. It hasn't connected the form yet, but now we've got the right destination ready. Leave this campaign open, because we're going to come back to it.
scenes.checkpoint: Wait until the saved campaign's connection setup opens.

scenes.title: Copy this campaign's address
scenes.narration: We've saved the offer, so now let's give Zapier the right destination. Choose Facebook or Instagram on this setup page. The private connection address here belongs to this campaign, which is how Patient Pipeline will know where this form's leads belong. Click Copy beside that address, and keep the campaign tab open while we set up Zapier. Don't use the normal page address from your browser, and don't put this private address in the ad. I'm hiding it in the lesson; when we get to the URL field, you'll paste your own full value.
scenes.checkpoint: Copy the special campaign address—not the browser's page URL.

scenes.title: Create a Zap and its trigger
scenes.narration: Now let's open Zapier in another browser tab and create a new Zap. I'll give it the name Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline, so we can recognize it later. A Zap starts with a trigger, which just means the event it's waiting for. Click that trigger step and choose Facebook Lead Ads as the app. For the event, choose New Lead. That's how we'll ask Zapier to watch for a new form response. Click Continue, and we'll connect the Facebook account that can actually see the Page and form we want.

fields.label: Zap name
fields.value: Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline

actions.result: Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline

scenes.checkpoint: Trigger app Facebook Lead Ads • event New Lead

scenes.title: Connect the correct Facebook account
scenes.narration: Now we're choosing which Facebook account Zapier can use. Open the account selection, and use an existing connection if it already has the access we need. Otherwise, choose the sign-in option and complete Facebook's own sign-in and permission prompts. Do that privately in your account; you don't need to share your password with anyone helping you. Once you're back in Zapier, check which account is selected, then continue. If your Page doesn't appear on the next screen, we'll come back and check access rather than accidentally choose another business.
scenes.checkpoint: Sign-in screens are not reproduced. Follow the real permission prompts.

scenes.title: Select the Page and exact form
scenes.narration: With the account connected, let's tell Zapier exactly which form belongs to this campaign. Open Page and choose the Facebook Page you wrote down. Then open Form and choose the Instant Form used by this particular ad. We don't want a broad selection that could send unrelated offers into the same campaign. Once both names look right, click Continue. Now we'll use Test trigger to find a sample from that form. We need a usable sample because, in a moment, we'll show Zapier which answers contain the person's name and phone.
scenes.checkpoint: Choose a specific Page AND Form. Generic sample data is not your live test.

scenes.title: Create an identifiable sample
scenes.narration: If there's no useful sample yet, we can make one with Meta's Lead Ads Testing Tool. Open it in another tab and select the same Page and Form. Click Preview Form, and fill it in with your own test details. Work through Next and Submit as the form asks, then close the preview and use Create lead as directed by the tool. That gives us setup data to work with. It isn't a live-ad check yet. We'll go back to Zapier next and make sure it finds the sample you actually entered, rather than an unrelated example.
scenes.checkpoint: developers.facebook.com/tools/lead-ads-testing/ • sample only, not live-ad proof.

scenes.title: Find that sample in Zapier
scenes.narration: Back in Zapier, click Test trigger again. When the results appear, select the sample that matches your details. Before we use it, make sure the phone and a usable name are actually present. If Meta says a test already exists and you need a new sample, its Delete lead control removes the testing tool's sample. That's the only sample we're talking about removing here, not a customer's real lead. Once you can identify your sample in Zapier, we're ready to tell the sending step which answers to use.
scenes.checkpoint: Do not use an invented generic sample as evidence of the form connection.

scenes.title: Add Webhooks by Zapier
scenes.narration: We've got a form response to work with, so now let's add the step that sends it to Patient Pipeline. Click the plus below the Facebook trigger, and choose Webhooks by Zapier as the action app. For its event, choose POST, then click Continue. We're using the ordinary POST action, not Custom Request, because it lets us enter the information in simple rows. You don't need to write code for this. We'll give it the campaign's private address first, and then match the name and phone answers from the form.
scenes.checkpoint: Webhooks by Zapier → POST

scenes.title: Paste the URL and choose JSON
scenes.narration: Let's get that destination again so we know we're using the right one. Switch to Patient Pipeline, check the campaign name, and click Copy beside its private address. Back in Zapier, click the URL box and paste it with Control V on Windows, or Command V on a Mac. Now choose JSON under Payload Type. That's just a format in the menu; it doesn't mean you need to type computer code. Leave the optional headers and authentication empty for this campaign address. Next we'll tell Zapier which form answers to send there.

fields.label: Headers / authentication
fields.value: Leave empty for this campaign address

scenes.checkpoint: URL from this campaign • Payload Type JSON

scenes.title: Match the name and phone fields
scenes.narration: Now we're matching the form answers to what Patient Pipeline expects. Under Data, type first underscore name in the left-hand box. On its right, open the field picker and choose the First Name answer from the Facebook trigger. That makes it change for each person, rather than always sending your test name. Add another row, and type phone on the left. Then choose the trigger's Phone Number answer on the right. Take a moment to compare both rows: labels on the left, changing form answers on the right. Don't type a fixed name or phone into those value boxes.
scenes.checkpoint: Left: first_name / phone • Right: dynamic form answers—not fixed test values.

scenes.title: If your form has only Full Name
scenes.narration: You might not see a separate First Name answer in your form, and that's okay. If it gives you Full Name instead, change that name key on the left to full underscore name. Then choose the form's Full Name answer on the right. Patient Pipeline can split that for you. Keep the phone row we just set up. We're replacing the first-name mapping here, not adding a second conflicting name rule. If you'd like to send email too, that's optional; use the email key with the actual Email answer from the trigger, rather than typing your own address.
scenes.checkpoint: Use either first_name or full_name, according to the fields your form supplies.

scenes.title: Test the sending action
scenes.narration: We've given Zapier its destination and matched the fields, so let's try the sending step. Check that the selected sample contains your approved test details, because this test really sends them into the campaign. Continue to the action's test step and send the sample. Then check Patient Pipeline for the same phone number. If the action reports an error, check the URL, JSON choice, and mapped name and phone. Even if this test succeeds, we haven't proved automatic delivery yet. We've checked the sending step; next we'll switch the Zap on and try a new form submission.
scenes.checkpoint: An action test can create a real lead. It is not end-to-end proof.

scenes.title: Publish and turn the Zap on
scenes.narration: Before we turn this on, let's look back over what we've connected. At the top, the Facebook Lead Ads trigger should use New Lead with your exact Page and Form. Beneath it, the Webhooks by Zapier action should use POST, your campaign address, and the mapped answers we just checked. When that's right, publish the Zap and confirm that it's on. The button wording may differ in your editor, but a saved draft isn't enough. Once it's active, a new matching submission can run through these steps without us pressing the test button.

fields.label: Trigger
fields.value: Facebook Lead Ads • New Lead • exact Page and Form

fields.label: Action
fields.value: Webhooks by Zapier • POST • JSON • mapped fields

scenes.checkpoint: Publish control is illustrative; confirm active status in your actual editor.

scenes.title: Now test a new real submission
scenes.narration: Now that the Zap is on, let's check the route a new lead will actually take. Open the same Instant Form through the actual ad, enter your own name and phone, and complete any required consent or verification. Submit once and wait for the form's confirmation. Then open Zap History in Zapier and look for a new run at the time you just submitted. Match its form details before we check Patient Pipeline. We're not rerunning the action test here. This new submission is what tells us whether the form starts the active Zap automatically.
scenes.checkpoint: New form submission after activation → new Zap run → campaign lead.

scenes.title: Check the receipt, then the lead
scenes.narration: Now let's return to that same campaign in Patient Pipeline and see what happened to your submission. Look for a recent Form submission received message. If it's still waiting, give it a moment and use your browser's refresh button to check again. Once you can see the receipt, open the campaign's Leads tab and look for the name and phone you used. We're matching your actual details here, not just looking for any new row. The illustration shows where to check; it isn't claiming your connection has passed. That confirmation needs to come from your own submission.

fields.label: Latest receipt
fields.value: Waiting for a submission from your form

scenes.checkpoint: No success is assumed. Find your own submission in this campaign.

scenes.title: Recognize a successful repeat test
scenes.narration: If you're testing again and don't see another row, that doesn't necessarily mean something went wrong. Open Lead sources and look under Last twenty received, then match the time to your test. A New lead result means a new entry was created. An Updated lead result can be successful too; that phone was already in this campaign, so Patient Pipeline updated the existing entry. It may not move to the top. If the receipt says Rejected, open it and read the reason before changing settings. That will tell us much more than repeatedly submitting and hoping.

fields.label: New lead
fields.value: A new campaign lead was created

fields.label: Updated lead
fields.value: Same campaign + same phone may update the existing lead

fields.label: Rejected
fields.value: Open the receipt and read the reason

scenes.checkpoint: Status explanations—not a fabricated delivery log.

scenes.title: Don't mistake an internal test for proof
scenes.page: Only want to check our side?
scenes.narration: There's one distinction I want to make before we finish, because it's easy to mistake a partial test for the whole connection working. Patient Pipeline's internal test checks its own intake. Testing a sending action checks that step, and it may create a real lead, but neither proves the actual form will trigger it automatically. That's why we've started our final check at the form itself and followed that same person's details into the campaign. Let your caller know which entry was your setup test, and keep private details out of any troubleshooting screenshots you share.

fields.label: Connector action test
fields.value: Can send real data; does not prove the trigger

scenes.checkpoint: Keep private details out of screenshots and shared troubleshooting messages.

scenes.title: If the lead is missing
scenes.narration: If your lead hasn't arrived, start with Zap History. When there's no new run, check that the Zap is on and watching the right Page and Form, and that Facebook leads access is still available. If there is a run but the action failed, open it and read the error. Then check the URL, JSON format, and dynamic name and phone answers. If Patient Pipeline says Updated lead, look for the existing entry with that phone. You don't need a new campaign to force another row. Fix the first failing part, then try the actual form again.

fields.value: Check On status, Page, Form, and leads access

fields.label: Failed action
fields.value: Read error; check URL, JSON, and dynamic values

fields.label: Updated lead
fields.value: Find the existing same-phone campaign lead

scenes.checkpoint: Fix the first failing step, then submit the actual form again.

scenes.title: Before you call it ready
scenes.narration: Before you leave the setup, take one more look at your campaign. Does it match the offer people actually saw? Good. Now make sure the connection is watching the right form and is switched on. The important part is what happened after you activated it: you submitted that actual form, and you found the matching receipt and lead in this campaign. If either part is missing, go back to that point before calling it ready. Leave the connection active, and let your team know which entry was your test. You now know where to look if a future delivery needs attention.
